newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Keppel T&T sees weaker 1997 results.
newsitem.headline: Keppel T&T sees weaker 1997 results.

text.p: Keppel Telecommunications & Transportation Ltd (Keppel T&T( said on Monday its 1997 results were likely to be lower due to start-up costs in its telecommunications business.

"The group expects a satisfactory performance in 1997 for its existing business activities. However, the group's results for the year are likely to be lower than the previous year in view of the share of start-up costs in MobileOne," a company statement accompanying its 1996 results said.
MobileOne (Asia) Pte Ltd is Keppel T&T's associate involved in cellular phone and paging services in Singapore which it will be launched in April.
Keppel T&T's net profit for year ended December 1996 rose 27.5 percent to Singapore $15.74 million.
Its turnover improved 35.2 percent to S$176.70 million due to growth in the telecommunications business, it said.
Keen competition dampened 1996 earnings from its shipping division, but charter income was expected to increase, Keppel T&T said. It would continue to increase the coverage of feeder routes.
The company proposed issuing up to 112.66 million new ordinary shares at Singapore $1.10 with up to 56.33 million warrants expiring in 2002.
The group said it planned to raise up to S$123.9 million for investments in its shipping, telecommunnications and logistics services.

The rights issue would be offered to shareholders on the basis of two rights shares for every four exisitng shares with every two rights shares being issued with one warrant carrying the right to subscribe for one new share.
The proposed rights issue will be managed by Keppel Bank of Singapore Ltd and co-managed by Keppel Securities Pte Ltd.
Analysts told Reuters the weaker contribution from the shipping business was within expectations while the high contribution from telecommunications was a pleasant surprise.
"The company's (short-term) earnings are not going to be great due to the high start-up cost of MobileOne," said an analyst with a U.S. house.
"If you buy the company's stocks, you would have to buy them for their potential earnings," the analyst said.
